page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with the running head and page number at the top. A short mark at the foot, the signature "P 2", and the catchword "Ex" at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: ollis inditur, leniori igne coquitur ex aqua butyro adiecto, aliquè pinguiusculo liquore: lautius fit autem, si carbonibus decoquatur ex iure gallinacei pulli aut gallinæ, saepè & diutius cochleari verfando, adiecto paulùm cinnamomi, zinzibe-ris modico, laudatiffimoq; faccharo, confert efum eruditatis ftomachi ex immodica crapula co-traëtis, iisq; qui à cibo largiori abstinere cupi-unt.
Huc pertinet panis diftillatus optimum nu-tritiuum & refectiuum, inter extra[?]ta nutritiua merito principem obtinens locum, tabidis morbo exhaustis conuenientissimum.
main_text.head: De panificiis quæ dicuntur placentæ.
main_text.p: AD panis categoriam proximè accedunt placentæ, Græcè πέμματα[?] & πλακοῦντης[?], & bellaria, quorum omnium rationem, numerum & differentias, nominaque conscribere infiniti esset operis.
Pro locorum enim & gentium varietate, temporum varia diuersitate & ratione variare ea certum est.

page.notes: The running head "PROROGANDA." is hard to read in the scan and may be misprinted. The Greek words in the placenta paragraph are doubtful: "πέμματα" and "πλακοῦντης" are marked [?]. "extraĕta" in the line "extra... nutritiua" is unclear. The first word "leniori" and "butyro" are copied as seen. The page number "227" is printed at the top right with a dash. The paragraph beginning "Huc pertinet" is set as its own paragraph and is not indented in the scan, but it follows a paragraph break. The final line ends with "est." where the printer may have set "eft."
